INSTRUCTIONS TO CANDIDATES: Answer ANY THREE questions. All questions carry equal marks. You are advised to spend the first fifteen minutes reading the paper. In calculations you are advised to show all the steps in your working. You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers. Calculators are allowed.
enonce_intro_markdown:

| Population | 40 |
| National income | 80 |
| Undistributed profit | 2 |
| Taxes on company profits | 1 |
| National social insurance contribution | 1.5 |
| Transfer payments received | 3 |
| Current price index | 160 |

Calculate the value of:
incertitudes: Question 4 (tableau) : la ligne « Population » est donnée dans une colonne intitulée « AMOUNT (Million FCFA) » ; la valeur 40 est utilisée telle qu'imprimée, sans unité propre, donc le revenu par tête vaut 80/40 = 2 millions de FCFA par habitant (lecture la plus probable de l'examinateur).

Question 4(a)(iii) : revenu réel par tête = 2 / 160 × 100 = 1,25 million de FCFA aux prix de l'année de base (indice de base 100) ; le sujet ne précise pas la base, 100 est l'hypothèse usuelle. Calculs vérifiés avec Python.
Question 4(a)(i) : revenu personnel = revenu national - bénéfices non distribués - impôts sur les sociétés - cotisations sociales + transferts = 78,5 millions de FCFA.

La consigne « Answer ANY THREE questions » est exprimée par regles_choix (3 parmi 5). Aucun total par question n'est imprimé (« All questions carry equal marks ») : `points` de l'exercice est laissé vide ; les `points` de chaque sous-question sont la somme des points imprimés de ses parties, et la somme imprimée de la question vaut 20.

questions.enonce_markdown:
(i) personal income. (4 marks)

(ii) per capita income. (4 marks)

(iii) real per capita income. (4 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i) Personal income.** Personal income is the income actually received by households. Starting from national income, we **subtract** the income that is earned but not received (undistributed company profits, taxes on company profits and social insurance contributions) and **add** transfer payments received:

$$\text{Personal income} = \text{National income} - \text{undistributed profit} - \text{taxes on company profits} - \text{social insurance contributions} + \text{transfer payments}$$

$$= 80 - 2 - 1 - 1.5 + 3 = 78.5 \text{ million FCFA}$$

**(ii) Per capita income.**

$$\text{Per capita income} = \frac{\text{National income}}{\text{Population}} = \frac{80}{40} = 2 \text{ million FCFA per head}$$

(The figures are used as printed in the table, population = 40.)

**(iii) Real per capita income.** Divide the nominal figure by the price index and multiply by 100 to remove the effect of price changes (the current price index is 160, with the base year = 100):

$$\text{Real per capita income} = \frac{\text{Per capita income}}{\text{Price index}} \times 100 = \frac{2}{160} \times 100 = 1.25 \text{ million FCFA per head}$$

Real per capita income is 1.25 million FCFA at base-year prices.

questions.enonce_markdown: How is personal income different from personal disposable income? (4 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
- **Personal income** is the **total income received by households** from all sources before any personal tax: wages and salaries, rent, interest, dividends and transfer payments. In (a)(i) it is 78.5 million FCFA.
- **Personal disposable income** is the part of personal income that households are **free to spend or save**, that is, personal income **after deducting personal direct taxes** (income tax and similar taxes paid by individuals):

$$\text{Personal disposable income} = \text{Personal income} - \text{personal direct taxes}$$

So personal income is always greater than (or equal to) personal disposable income; the difference is the direct taxes paid by individuals. Example (hypothetical): if households pay 8 million FCFA in income tax, disposable income is $78.5 - 8 = 70.5$ million FCFA.

questions.enonce_markdown: List four factors that will lead to an increase in living standards of an economy. (4 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
Four factors (1 mark each, any four):

1. **Economic growth:** a rise in real national output and real income per head, so more goods and services per person.
2. **Better education and health care**, which raise the quality and productivity of the labour force and improve well-being.
3. **Investment in capital, infrastructure and improved technology**, which raise productivity and output (roads, electricity, water supply).
4. **A more equal distribution of income**, so that growth benefits a wider part of the population.
5. **Stable prices** (low inflation) which protect the purchasing power of incomes.
6. **Political stability and good governance**, and **control of population growth** so that output grows faster than the population.
